title: security(rbac-v2): enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Asha Rao
release_notes: Enforce KMS key region pinning for RBAC v2 resources; augment audit logs with KMS key and residency metadata; backward-compatible migrations; no user-visible API changes.
description: Motivation: closing a compliance gap where RBAC v2 policies allowed creating resources bound to customer-managed KMS keys in regions not permitted by the project's residency policy. This change enforces KMS region pinning at policy evaluation time, surfaces clear audit logs for KMS usage, and hardens audit metadata to assist compliance investigations. Summary of changes: 1) policy enforcer: validate kmsKey.region against resource.residency.allowed_regions and deny or require explicit override via admin-only flag; 2) audit pipeline: add kms_key_id, kms_key_region, and residency_reason fields to audit events; 3) migration: add a non-blocking scanner to detect existing resources with mismatched residency/KMS region and emit findings to the security workspace; 4) e2e and CI: integration tests that exercise policy deny/allow flows and audit propagation. Backwards compatibility: checks are enforced only for accounts with RBACv2 enabled and for resources that opt into residency controls (default on for new orgs). Existing orgs will see alert findings but not automatic deletion. Rollout plan: staged rollout with feature flag (rbac_v2_kms_region_enforcement) -> soft enforcement (alerts only) -> hard enforcement after 2 weeks and signoff from compliance. Ops runbook included for emergency rollback. Testing: unit tests + integration tests added; manual QA with example KMS keys across regions; security scan run and warnings cleared. Impact: reduces risk of cross-region data residency violations and improves forensic traceability for KMS usage. See linked Linear items for acceptance criteria and compliance team signoff.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can we also enforce this in the API layer as a defensive check? If enforcer is bypassed somehow we should reject at the API boundary.
Asha Rao: We added an API-layer validation in services/iam/api_v2/validate_kms.go (small fail-safe). Enforcer remains the source of truth for policy evaluation.
Priya Nair: Needs a migration plan for existing keys in disallowed regions — do not auto-fix. Recommend alerting + bulk export for remediation.
Asha Rao: Added scan_kms_residency.go to enumerate mismatches and produce findings for SOC. Migration script is non-destructive by design.
Carlos Mendes: Audit fields look good, but ensure PII-safe — do not include customer email or plaintext key material in logs.
Asha Rao: Audit producer only includes kms key resource id and region; key material is never logged. Confirmed with security scan.
Liam Chen: Integration tests flake on 5% of runs due to test KMS latency. Can we add retry/backoff to the test harness?
Asha Rao: Added retries and increased timeouts in the integration job. Observed stability improvement in CI runs.
ci_checks: e2e: pass (flaky KMS tests stabilized with retries)
notes_for_ops: Feature flag controls rollout: rbac_v2_kms_region_enforcement. Default deploy is soft enforcement (alerts only). To enable hard enforcement set the flag to 'on' in the control plane and verify 'migration_scan:clear' in the security workspace. Emergency rollback: revert the flag to 'off' and redeploy audit producer if necessary.
qa_steps: Create org with residency controls enabled and attempt to create resource with KMS key in disallowed region => expect 403 policy denied
Create resource in allowed region with valid KMS key => expect success and audit event with kms_key_id and kms_key_region
Run migration scanner against existing orgs => expect findings and exportable CSV
Toggle feature flag to soft enforcement => verify alerts only (no create deny)
Toggle feature flag to hard enforcement => verify denies are enforced and metrics increment
